title: Unlocking the Anticancer Potential of New Spirooxindoles via p53-MDM2/MDMX Dual Inhibition: In Vitro and In Silico Assessments.
authors: El-Zoheiry, Haidy H; Ahmed, Rehab F; Elkotamy, Mahmoud S; Abdel-Aziz, Hatem A; Elmasry, Ghada F
one_liner_zh: 该文研究小分子抑制剂阻断p53-MDM2/MDMX蛋白-蛋白互作，虽含分子对接与MD模拟，但对象为蛋白-蛋白而非蛋白-DNA互作，与本课题TF-DNA结合机制无关。
abstract: Blocking the p53-MDM2 and/or p53-MDMX protein-protein interaction (PPI) by small-molecule inhibitors has been tracked as a potentially effective cancer treatment approach. Herein, we present the discovery of a new series of spirooxindole-tethered pyrazolopyridine derivatives. The development of the new congeners was based on the analysis of the co-crystal structures of the inhibitors bound to both MDM2 and MDMX and studying the binding interactions between the substituents of small molecules and the three subpockets of the p53-MDM2/MDMX. The spirooxindoles 6b, 6k, and 6n attained the most pronounced activity in the MULTI-ARRAY MDM2-p53 complex assay with IC(50) values of 1.26, 1.30, and 1.25 microM, respectively, in comparison with nutlin-3 (IC(50) = 2.03 microM). The counterparts 6b, 6k, and 6n also revealed notable inhibitory potential against p53-MDMX. The antiproliferative efficacy of the most active target compounds was assessed in HCT-116 colon cancer cell line that overexpressed MDM2 and harbored wild-type p53. The derivative 6k accomplished the highest antiproliferative activity against HCT-116 compared to nutlin-3. Moreover, 6k displayed minimal toxicity compared to the reference nutlin-3 when examined on a normal cell line. Flow cytometric analysis revealed that 6k controlled cell growth via cell cycle arrest at the G1 phase and induced cell death via apoptosis. Additionally, compound 6k revealed a prominent effect in raising p53 levels with a 6.464-fold increase compared to the control. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations justified the observed efficacy. Collectively, this study showcased a new class of potent p53-MDM2/MDMX dual inhibitors possessing a spirooxindole scaffold which can be subjected to future development.
abstract_zh: 通过小分子抑制剂阻断p53-MDM2和/或p53-MDMX蛋白-蛋白相互作用（PPI）已被视为一种潜在有效的癌症治疗方法。在此，我们报告了一系列新型螺环吲哚酮-四氢吡唑并吡啶衍生物的发现。新同系物的开发基于对抑制剂与MDM2和MDMX结合共晶结构的分析，并研究了小分子取代基与p53-MDM2/MDMX三个亚口袋之间的结合相互作用。在MULTI-ARRAY MDM2-p53复合物实验中，螺环吲哚酮6b、6k和6n表现出最显著的活性，其IC(50)值分别为1.26、1.30和1.25微摩尔，与nutlin-3（IC(50) = 2.03微摩尔）相比。对应化合物6b、6k和6n也显示出对p53-MDMX的显著抑制潜力。在过表达MDM2且携带野生型p53的HCT-116结肠癌细胞系中评估了最具活性目标化合物的抗增殖效力。与nutlin-3相比，衍生物6k对HCT-116实现了最高的抗增殖活性。此外，在正常细胞系上检测时，6k与参考化合物nutlin-3相比显示出极低的毒性。流式细胞术分析揭示，6k通过G1期细胞周期阻滞控制细胞生长，并通过凋亡诱导细胞死亡。另外，化合物6k在提高p53水平方面表现出显著效果，与对照相比增加了6.464倍。分子对接和分子动力学模拟验证了观察到的效力。总体而言，本研究展示了一类新型强效p53-MDM2/MDMX双抑制剂，其具有螺环吲哚酮骨架，可用于未来开发。
